judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the payload lacks a refresh_token, and callers persist that result directly into credential.key. Google CalendarService.ts (~line 93) and Office365CalendarService.ts (~line 258) write the parsed object to prisma.credential.update — the user's real OAuth refresh token in the DB is replaced with the junk string "refresh_token", which is irreversible: the stored credential can never be refreshed again and the user must manually re-authorize the app. This also fires in the credential-sync path, where the sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token + expiry, so every synced refresh destroys the stored refresh token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed payload lacks `refresh_token`, the helper forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which will overwrite the existing stored `refresh_token` with the literal string when Microsoft (or the credential-sync endpoint) doesn’t return a refresh token. That updated object is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, causing irreversible loss of the real refresh token. (Google’s code path passes an object that already contains `refresh_token`, so the overwrite claim is less directly supported there, but the overwrite/persist defect is clearly present for Office365 and any sync responses without `refresh_token`.)
